result.title: When Should a Voice Agent Speak? End-of-Turn Detection in Turkish
result.summary: A voice agent that waits for a fixed silence before replying either interrupts users who pause mid-utterance or responds late to users who have finished. This study examines the decision at the onset of silence, using turn ends and turn-internal pauses extracted from the Real-TurnTurk corpus of Turkish dyadic video calls. A fine-tuned Turkish TurnGPT model, a zero-shot Turkish language model and a deployed multilingual detector are compared, together with voice-activity timing and facial features, under recording-disjoint and speaker-disjoint evaluation with paired cluster bootstrap tests. On held-out recordings, the fine-tuned model separates turn ends from pauses better than both text baselines and is the best calibrated of the three. Timing features of the current speaker are similarly informative, and their combination with the fine-tuned text score gives the best timing-based results; with logistic regression, this combination also outperforms the same combination with either text baseline. In a latency simulation, adding the text score to a silence timeout shortens the mean response delay at the same interruption rate. On automatic Whisper transcripts, the fine-tuned model retains its advantage over the zero-shot model.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究土耳其语语音助手在静音起始时应否开口的问题，从真实双人视频通话语料中区分轮次结束与轮内停顿，比较微调 TurnGPT、零样本语言模型与多语种检测器，并结合发声时序与面部特征，在录音/说话人分离设定下评估，还做了延迟模拟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是「何时继续等待、何时终止」的停止决策与停止信号校准，可能为 LVR 中 STOP 判据（如从部分状态判断是否已获足够证据）提供概念类比，但模态与任务距离较远，需核查其校准与延迟—错误权衡的度量方式。
